full_judgment: 15. It appears from the evidence on record and from the observation of the learned trial court that it based its findings on circumstantial evidence and confession of the accused Akbor Ali recorded U/S 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. There is no rule of law that if there be no eye witness to a murder the accused should not be sentenced to death. It is not difficult to procure false evidence of eye witness. It is on the other hand extremely difficult to produce circumstantial evidence of a convincing character and therefore, circumstantial evidence if convincing is more cogent than the evidence of eye witness. The learned A.A.G. has tried to convince us to the effect that the deceased filed a criminal case against the accused Akbor Ali and as such he (Akbor Ali) has committed the crime by murdering the deceased with the help of his associates which finds support in the statement of the confessing accused Akbor Ali vide Ext. 7. In this connection it may not be out of place to mention here that it is the persistent case of the prosecution that deceased Motijan had illegal affairs with the accused Akbor Ali and during the life time of her husband Lal Mia /P.W.5 the deceased used to live with Akbor as husband and wife and even she along with Akbor filed case against her brother P.W. 1 and her husband. The deceased Motijan even filed a case against Akbor Ali on the allegation of rape with whom she admittedly used to reside and for which several salish took place. It is more curious that the I.O. has found that the accused Akbor made a confessional statement regarding murder of the deceased and curious enough that the confessing accused found to have said that he along with Ahmed, Johur Ali, Ratiqul, Sattar, Rahim, Haider son of Johur Ali murdered the deceased but I.O. has failed  to bring said Ahmed, Johur Ali, Rafiqul. Sattar and Rahim either as witness or accused so it appears that the I.O. himself was not satisfied about the genuineness of the confessional statement of the accused Akbor Ali vide Ext. 7. In this case it may not out to place to mention here that the prosecution has failed to bring any iota of evidence against the rest accused appellant Md. Haider Ali who happens to be the son of Jahur Ali. The confessional statement Ext.7 of the confessing accused bears the reference of one Haider Ali son of Janab Ali who is neither witness nor accused in this case. The neighbours as well as the persons who allegedly took part in the occurrence as per confessional statement of the accused Akbor Ali are the relevant witnesses and non examination of any of them as witness or bringing them on dock as accused create presumption U/S 114 (g) of the Evidence Act and raises a question of doubt in the prosecution and benefit of this defect would go to the accused. Moreover the Magistrate P.W. 13 who recorded the confessional statement of the confessing accuse Akbor Ali has failed to satisfy us as to its truth and voluntariness since he failed to ask the confessing accused as to whether he was tortured during custody or that he gave any understanding to the confessing accused that whether he confess or not, will not be handed over to police custody. So in all practical purpose it appears that the formalities as provided under Section 164 and 364 have not be complied with in recording the confessional statement of accused Akbor. Moreover, it appears that the confessing accused made the confessional statement after coming from remand which in no way remove to doubt that it is (Confessional Statement Ext. 7) the product of threat, coercion and physical torture. More so there is no independent evidence to corroborate the same. Finally the confessional statement Ext. 7 appears to be exculpatory having no active part in the occurrence by the confessing accused and as such the same (Ext 7) cannot be used against its maker and the confessing accused Akbor Ali cannot be convicted on the basis of it. Before parting with this record we must observe that the learned trial court most illegally convicted the accused Haider Ali on the basis of Ext. 7 but it appears there from that there is a reference of one Haider son of Jonab Ali but the present accused appellant at serial No. 2 is the son of Johur Ali and not Jonab Ali. So there is a great doubt as to whether the accused Haider Ali son of Johur Ali is the same person as referred to in Ext. 7 who took part in the occurrence and benefit of this defect would go to the accused. All these facts and circumstances led us to hold that the confessional statement Ext. 7 is not a confession in the eye of law and the same cannot be the basis of conviction. In view of such facts and circumstances, we are led to hold that there is absolutely no legal evidence against the accused persons which justify the submission of the learned Advocate for appellants.
